findings.title: The new version runs 370 of the 382 rules of four commonly used packs (typescript 0.1.7, python 0.1.9, complexity 0.1.7, javascript 0.1.8)
findings.what: A person who keeps today's packs (typescript 0.1.7, python 0.1.9, complexity 0.1.7, javascript 0.1.8) gets 12 rules fewer: the engine skips each rule whose token test reads a token the new tape may leave out, and says so in the daemon log. Set-up still says 382 rules; the session's start says 370. The 12: eslint-no-self-assign, eslint-no-sparse-arrays, eslint-no-unexpected-multiline, eslint-no-with, ruff-f633-invalid-print-syntax, ruff-ruf008-mutable-dataclass-default, ruff-ruf009-function-call-in-dataclass-default-argument, ruff-ruf013-implicit-optional, ruff-sim905-split-static-string, ruff-up034-extraneous-parentheses, typescript-eslint-no-require-imports, typescript-eslint-prefer-namespace-keyword. They come back once their packs are republished for the new engine.
findings.severity: medium: findings a person had at 0.1.5 are not made until the packs are republished; set-up's count (382) does not match what runs (370)

findings.title: TypeScript rules on real code take twice as long: 7.2 s at 0.1.5, 14.7 s at the new version
findings.what: The typescript pack (65 rules) over Rerail's own 600 TypeScript files: wall time cold 7.24 s to 14.68 s (2.03 times; 1.93 in three confirmation runs), warm 1.96 times, CPU 1.86 times; peak memory the same (578 to 595 MB). One rule makes most of it: typescript-eslint-no-shadow alone takes 3.21 s at 0.1.5 and 9.29 s at the new version, 6.1 s of the 7.4 s gap. The pack fails the branch's own bar of 1.10 times.
findings.severity: high: a person whose repository uses the TypeScript pack waits twice as long for a scan

findings.title: The new version misses 6 no-shadow findings that 0.1.5 reports on Rerail's own tests
findings.what: On the same 600 files the two versions agree on 10,778 typescript findings; 6 are reported by 0.1.5 only, all typescript-eslint-no-shadow in test/engine/code-rule/code-rule-bridge.test.ts (lines 119, 160, 245 among them). They are real shadows as ESLint's rule defines them: an arrow parameter resolve hides `import { resolve } from "node:path"` (lines 119, 160), and `let opened` hides the module's function opened (line 245). Every other pack agrees finding for finding (javascript 36,579, node 2,753, rust 965, complexity 347, rerail 7).
findings.severity: medium: true findings lost on real code; the branch's fixtures check does not see them

findings.title: Four packs are faster on real code at the new version, and javascript uses 30% less memory
findings.what: Wall time cold, new against 0.1.5: rust 4.74 s to 3.65 s (0.77 times), javascript 13.25 s to 10.94 s (0.83), complexity 0.88, rerail 0.89. The javascript pack's peak memory falls from 1,232 MB to 859 MB. node is at the bar: 10.95 s to 12.01 s (1.10 times), CPU 1.09.

findings.title: The bar's own summary hides the slow rule: it says no rule is slower in total
findings.what: report.md names the typescript slowdown's biggest contributor as 'no rule slower in total (-9.82 s over 65 rules)'. Its own table below shows typescript-eslint-no-shadow +6.08 s. The hint adds each rule's time alone, and every other rule alone runs about 0.25 s faster at the new version (the corpus's fixed cost in each one-rule run), so the 64 savings cancel the one slow rule. A maintainer reading the summary line would look in the wrong place.
findings.severity: low: a defect of the report text in scripts/ship

findings.title: The typescript gap holds at every corpus size and core count measured: 1.7 to 2.0 times
findings.what: typescript pack, wall time cold, 0.1.5 to the new version. Corpus size at 4 cores: 226 files 3.44 s to 5.86 s (1.70 times), 600 files 7.24 to 14.68 (2.03), 2,312 files 9.30 to 18.23 (1.96). Cores on the 600 files: 1 core 17.0 to 29.8 s (1.75), 4 cores 7.24 to 14.68 (2.03), 8 cores 7.09 to 12.66 (1.79). 0.1.5 gains nothing past 4 cores (7.2 s to 7.1 s); the new version gains 14% (14.7 s to 12.7 s). The node pack sits at the bar everywhere: 1.03 times at 1 core, 1.10 at 4, 0.99 at 8 cores (where its CPU is 1.18 times and its peak memory 1.22 times 0.1.5's, 629 to 768 MB), 1.14 on 226 files and 1.10 on 2,312.
findings.severity: high: the slowdown is not an effect of one corpus or one machine size

findings.title: A fresh daemon's first event in a 153-checkout repository: 7.7 s at the new version, 7.2 s at 0.1.5, 1.0 s at main + six fixes
findings.what: One repository of 153 checkouts of 7,502 files, set up and started (382 rules set up), the daemon started fresh, four sessions in a stopped checkout sending a tool call's two hooks every 4 s; 60 s in, one session's SessionStart in the large repository, then a tool call every 20 s, for 300 s. The first PreToolUse after the SessionStart waited 7.67 s at the new version, 7.23 s at 0.1.5 and 1.01 s at B; the daemon gave no answer for 7.2 s at the new version and 6.6 s at 0.1.5, and never over 1 s at B. Peak resident memory 2.5, 2.4 and 2.7 GB; the daemon's CPU over the 120 s after the first event 122%, 118% and 105% of one core. Hooks of the other sessions in the first 300 s: p95 299 ms at the new version, 373 ms at 0.1.5, 171 ms at B; worst 2.1, 2.1 and 0.2 s. One run each.
findings.severity: medium: the new version keeps 0.1.5's stall here; the fixes we hold remove it

findings.title: Upgrading from 0.1.5 costs no more than a restart: the first event after the upgrade waits 8.2 s
findings.what: The same repository set up by 0.1.5, its daemon stopped, then the new version's daemon started on that home with its content store empty (the store moves from content-v1.sqlite to content-v4.sqlite, so nothing of 0.1.5's is read): start 3.8 s; the first hooks in a small started repository 1.17 s (SessionStart), then 0.15 to 0.18 s; the large repository's first PreToolUse 8.17 s, a 7.2 s silence, peak 2.5 GB, as a fresh daemon of the new version on its own home (7.67 s, 7.2 s). The old store stays on disk (2 MB here; its file is not removed). One run.

findings.title: The new version records every audit as failed while the 12 rules are skipped, and stores 207 KB of rule provenance per checkout: the database grows from 0.4 MB to 35 MB on one session's first event
findings.what: After the large repository's first event the new version's database held 153 audits, one per checkout, each with status failed and 12 failures (code adapter-error: 'policy rule eslint-no-self-assign (rerail) is skipped: a token test reads a token the tape may leave out...'), and 153 rule provenance rows of 207 KB each (31.5 MB). rerail.sqlite went from 0.40 MB to 35.0 MB (34.6 MB after the upgrade run). 0.1.5 and our build wrote no audit in the same run: their databases ended at 0.45 MB. In the small repository each of 5 sessions added one failed audit (one provenance row shared). rerail status does not mention the failures, and the agent is not told.
findings.severity: high: a person with many worktrees gets a database that grows by about 0.2 MB per checkout and a failed audit per session and checkout, with no word of why

findings.title: The rules the branch names as slow, timed alone: no-shadow 2.6 times, the node builtins rule 1.15 times, n-no-deprecated-api 1.06 times
findings.what: Each rule alone over the 600-file corpus, 3 rounds a side, medians (wall; in-process compile and evaluate). typescript-eslint-no-shadow 3.81 s to 10.07 s (evaluate 3.25 to 9.48 s) and 98 findings against 104. n-no-unsupported-features-node-builtins 7.39 s to 8.53 s: its compile alone is 1.74 s at 0.1.5 and 2.21 s at the new version, its evaluate 5.05 to 5.57 s. n-no-deprecated-api 3.58 to 3.80 s. A typical rule is faster at the new version (n-no-process-exit 0.97 to 0.70 s, typescript-eslint-no-use-before-define 1.58 to 1.31 s); the empty rule set costs 0.56 s on both. The branch's own figures (no-shadow 3.7 s to 12.1 s; the two node rules) hold on this machine.
findings.severity: high for no-shadow, low for the node rules

findings.title: The final-shape engine itself is far slower and heavier on a first run: killed at 24 GB on javascript, 46 times 0.1.5 on typescript, 6.8 times on node; a second run on the same files takes under a second
findings.what: No setting of the product turns the final-shape engine on for shipped packs: it runs .rr rules (rerail rules test, rerail-engine run-policies), and the branch keeps the present engine for every shipped pack. Its own run over the same 600 files, through the bar's .rr side, against 0.1.5's product path: javascript (123 rewrites) used over 24 GB and was ended by the memory cap after 235 s (0.1.5: 13.3 s, 1.2 GB); typescript took 322.5 s, 942 s of CPU and 11.0 GB on its first run (0.1.5: 7.0 s, 0.6 GB); node 73.1 s and 1.1 GB (0.1.5: 10.8 s, 0.6 GB). Warm, on its own content store with nothing changed, the same runs take 0.54 s (node) and 1.03 s (typescript). The engine refuses 8 node rewrites ('no columns for spec_resolved', 'tsconfig_for is read, and nothing derives it') and 1 typescript rewrite (triple-slash-reference); they were left out.
findings.severity: informative for this pull request (cutover is not part of it); high for any plan to move shipped packs to the final-shape engine

findings.title: Under the 10-minute load 0.1.5's daemon holds a full core: 98% on average, hooks at 8.3 s p95
findings.what: 0.1.5 under the load of 190 worktrees, 17 started repositories and 8 sessions with 26 tool-call streams (10 minutes, after a 2-minute warm-up): daemon CPU 98% of one core on average and 111% in the busiest minute, heap after a forced collection +14.3 MB a minute, resident memory rising 79.5 MB a minute, hook p95 8.31 s against a floor of 0.11 s, slowest hook 14.5 s; no hook failed or was lost, and the daemon answered all 50 probes. The CPU profile at minute 9: 36% of the main thread in Git processes started (readGit, run), 10% in file walks. The same load for N and B is not measured yet (see not measured).
findings.severity: context: the baseline a person has today

findings.title: Under the load, the daemon's cost is not in the rules: N with no rule pack in 16 of 17 repositories still holds 93% of a core
findings.what: the new version's load run set up 16 of its 17 repositories with no rule pack (one with 59 rules) and still averaged 93% of one core (busiest minute 107%), hooks 7.6 s at p95 and 18.3 s at worst; 0.1.5 with 323 rules in each Python repository: 98%, 111%, 8.3 s, 14.5 s. Both CPU profiles at minute 9 put Git processes started first among named causes (N 28.5% of the main thread, 0.1.5 36.1%). the new version's heap stayed flat (0.7 MB a minute against 14.3) and its memory lower (1,072 against 1,817 MB), which fewer compiled rules may explain. The two runs do not compare as a pair; a run of the new version with the same packs as 0.1.5 is needed to say more.
findings.severity: context: the new version does not lift the daemon's load cost; the measure of the new version with its rules is still to make
